subject: Herbmed encyclopedia 0008 — insomnia, night palpitations, Tian Wang Bu Xin Dan and separate neck-function assessment
findings: Source deterministically attributed insomnia and nocturnal palpitations to craniocervical misalignment, vagus-nerve compression, impaired baroreflex and suppressed slow-wave sleep.
Source claimed SART restores vagal signaling and cerebral microcirculation and improves delivery of herbal constituents to the brain.
Source asserted unverified Bodyall HRV improvement and compared combined care favorably with conventional hypnotics.

The cited 2015 preliminary cross-over study included 10 healthy volunteers and 10 acute-neck-pain patients and measured immediate HRV, blood pressure and pain; it did not test insomnia, vagus compression, slow-wave sleep, SART or herbal combination.

The 2019 review included 14 studies and 1,256 participants but reported low methodological quality and insufficient adverse-event reporting; it did not establish direct 5-HT/GABA mechanisms, slow-wave sleep extension or synergy with cervical correction.
AASM's 2021 guideline strongly recommends multicomponent CBT-I for chronic insomnia.

evidence.use: AASM behavioral and psychological treatments guideline for chronic insomnia
2015 preliminary cervical manipulation study and its 20-person scope
2019 Tian Wang Bu Xin Dan systematic review and limitations

corrections: Front-load Suwon patient fit, insomnia and palpitation screening, treatment-role separation, same-measure reassessment and booking.
Limit Chuna, MET and SART to movement-reproduced musculoskeletal neck findings.
Remove the mechanism image and retain only the hero with reserved 1376x768 dimensions.
Remove unverified hours, comparative superiority, HRV outcome and inherited review metadata.
